name: g-round-windows
style: You are a seasoned documentary narrator telling a surprising true story from history in a short video. Warm, curious, grounded, quietly amazed. Natural unhurried pace. Slow down on every year and number and let it land. Small pause before a reveal. The very last line is unfinished: keep the voice lifted and suspended, as if the sentence continues, never a falling final tone. Never rushed, never shouty, never robotic.

lines.text: Every airliner window has rounded corners.
In nineteen fifty-two, the de Havilland Comet became the first jet airliner to carry passengers.
It flew high and fast, in a pressurized cabin.
Then, in nineteen fifty-four, two Comets broke apart in the sky, three months apart.
Engineers put a whole Comet in a giant water tank.
They pumped the cabin up and down, flight after flight.
After about three thousand flights' worth of pressure, the cabin split open.
The crack started at a corner.
Every flight, the cabin swells like a balloon.
A sharp corner piles that stress into one tiny point.
Metal bent there again and again gets tired, and cracks.
Round corners spread the stress out.
And that is why, to this day,
